The resident expert on vegetarian cooking and food science, she has developed popular recipes such as Indian butter chickpeas and spinach puffs, and starred in short technical cooking videos which have garnered over 15M views across social media. Her hit article "8 Reasons You Should Never Eat Baby Carrots," has been read by over 2M people.Before joining Delish, Taylor Ann worked as a line cook in NYC, most notably at abcV, and as a freelance recipe developer and children’s theater teacher. Today she also keeps busy writing her own free weekly newsletter, Mostly Vegetarian, and maintaining her cooking blog, project cookbook. When she’s not dreaming up new recipes, she's listening to podcasts, drinking coffee, and taking long walks with her husband.

name: Watergate Salad
recipeIngredient: 1 (20-oz.) can crushed pineapple, drained, plus 1/2 cup pineapple liquid
Finely chopped or crushed roasted, salted pistachios and/or maraschino cherries with stems, for serving (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk pineapples, pineapple liquid, and pudding until combined and slightly thickened, about 1 minute.
Fold in marshmallows and Cool Whip until no streaks of pudding remain and marshmallows are dispersed.
Transfer pineapple mixture to a serving bowl. Loosely cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until marshmallows soften, at least 4 hours and, preferably, up to overnight.
Uncover and top with pistachios and cherries (if using).

comment.text: I've had this before and find it very presentible as a dinner party compliment. Swirl cool whip on top, sprinkle crushed nuts, garnish top with a few marichino cherries. Vey pretty and DELISH!!
Best salad ever. Everyone loved it

review.reviewBody: Served this yesterday (Thanksgiving)  with the cherries sprinkled along with the nuts on top of the cool whip....loved by all. This is a fast and just DELISH! go to compliment for any party.
